subject: ventures/hardwood-refinishing-bid-calculator
professional: a hardwood floor refinishing contractor/estimator who bids sand-and-finish and screen-and-recoat jobs and has to know crew-hours, finish gallons and margin before sending a number

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test calc.test.mjs` etc. and a scratch script against calc.mjs, then recomputed by hand. (1) Default 800 sq ft + 12 treads + 2 closets, full sand, poly: field 8*8=64h, stairs 12*0.4=4.8h, closets 2h, furniture 3h, repair 1.5h = 75.3h; loaded wage 42*1.3=54.60; labor 4111.38; finish area 800+12*4=848; 848*3/450=5.65 -> 6 gal*$85=510; supplies 8.48*18=152.64; direct 4111.38+662.64+185=4959.02; +15% overhead = 5702.87; /0.75 = 7603.83 (tool: 7603.83, 75.30h, 6 gal). Matches the README and page figure, $9.50/sq ft (7603.83/800=9.505). (2) Same job with stain: stain 8.48*1.8=15.264h -> 90.564h; stain gal ceil(848/500)=2 ($90); cost 90.564*54.6+510+90+152.64+185=5882.43; *1.15=6764.80; /0.75=9019.73 (tool: 9019.73). (3) 400 sq ft screen preset (3.5h/100, 2 coats): 14+2+0.5=16.5h; labor 900.90; 2 gal=170, supplies 72, +185 = 1327.90; *1.15 = 1527.09; /0.75 = 2036.11 (tool: 2036.11). (4) Stairs-trap preset share: 5.6h of 33.1h = 16.9%, matches the page's 'more than 15%' claim. Margin is correctly a share of price (cost/(1-m)), not a markup. Inputs validated: 'abc', negative wage, negative burden/margin all throw; margin>=100 rejected. Arithmetic is right; capped at 3 because the hours defaults are unsourced (see domain).
evidence.completeness: Checked every feature in README/page: field/stairs/closets takeoff (works), screen vs full sand presets (works, auto-updates hours unless edited), stain and color-change extra coat (works), loaded labour/overhead/margin (works), walk-away price, price/sq ft, stair hour share (all in calculateBid output), Copy bid summary (formatBidSummary tested), proposal builder with deposit/valid-days (proposal.mjs, 42 tests), share links (share.mjs), opt-out usage tally honouring DNT/GPC (usage.mjs), three SEO pages. No TODO/FIXME in any .mjs (grep count 0). README limitations are stated (one house, single labour rate, no tax). VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype with all hypotheses untested, consistent. Not marked 4: README does not mention the proposal/share features that exist.
evidence.verification: `node --test` per file: calc 16/16, page 11/11, proposal 42/42, share 10/10, usage 6/6, vs-flat 8/8, vs-jobber 9/9 (all pass; `node --test` with no args per README was not used, files run individually). Mutation 1: changed price = totalCost / (1 - targetMargin/100) to totalCost * (1 + targetMargin/100) in calc.mjs; calc+proposal tests went 3 failures (55 pass, 3 fail) so the margin-vs-markup core is caught. Mutation 2: Math.ceil -> Math.floor in gallonCount; calc.test.mjs 4 failures (12 pass, 4 fail). Both reverted with git checkout (git status clean). The golden test pins 7603.83 and 75.30h. Gap: no test pins that baseCoats should change labour (it does not), and no property tests; tests mostly assert the author's own numbers.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs in full, skimmed proposal.mjs/share.mjs/usage.mjs and index.html script. calc.mjs is a clean pure module: small validator, all inputs checked with named errors, JSDoc'd, no DOM, no silent fallbacks, zero-division guards on shares. Defects: `input.x ?? 0` defaults mean a missing required rate silently prices at zero for wage/finishCost/overhead rather than erroring (only the allowZero:false fields throw); stairs ignore method and coat count; 4 sq ft/tread is a hard-coded constant not exposed in the UI; index.html is a 48 KB single file with inline script, acceptable for the no-build design. No dead code found.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'no network calls' - grep for fetch/XMLHttpRequest/sendBeacon in index.html and non-test .mjs found none; privacy/localStorage key and DNT/GPC opt-out backed by usage.mjs + usage.test.mjs; '$7,603.83 / $9.50 / 75.30h / $5,702.87' backed by calc.test.mjs and my recompute; 'Copy summary omits wages and costs' backed by formatBidSummary (reads right) ; disclaimer present in README and index.html line 271; MIT LICENSE present. Weak points: README/page say sand-and-stain is 'several hundred dollars more' - actual delta is $1,415.90 (9019.73 vs 7603.83), i.e. understated, not wrong in direction; llms.txt links point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of marisstella.app; vs-jobber.html public copy says "Jobber's own site is not reachable from this session", an agent-process leak into customer-facing text; the pages' 'walk-away price below which the job loses money' equals total cost incl. overhead, which is accurate as defined.
evidence.fitness: Walked an estimator through the job: enter 800 sq ft, 12 treads, 2 closets, pick method/stain, overwrite wage/costs with real invoices, read price, hours, walk-away, compare a competitor's number, copy a bid summary or build a proposal. That works end to end and the stair-share and walk-away views are genuinely useful. A working contractor would hit gaps in the first hour: only one blended labour rate (no sander vs helper), stair hours do not change with method or coats (a stained 3-coat stair costs the same hours as a screen-and-recoat stair), changing base coats from 1 to 5 changes materials only (price 7082.50 vs 8125.16, hours stay 75.30) so more coats never adds labour, no multiple floors/levels, no minimum-job or contingency line, no dust-containment/subfloor-repair options, no sales tax. Hence 2.
evidence.domain: Method (hours per 100 sq ft by task, gallons = area*coats/coverage rounded up, loaded wage, overhead on direct cost, margin on price) matches standard contractor estimating practice and NWFA-style coverage (450 sq ft/gal/coat finish, 500 stain are in the normal 400-600 band). Departures a senior refinisher would flag: (a) 4 sq ft per tread-plus-riser is low for a 40 in. stair (about 3 sq ft tread + 2 sq ft riser, roughly 5); (b) 0.4 h per tread (24 min) is well under what most refinishers use (commonly priced $40-$100+ per tread, 45-90 min) and does not scale with sanding vs screening; (c) labour does not scale with coat count, and there is no dry-time or multi-day mobilisation effect; (d) gallons round to whole gallons, ignoring 5-gal pail pricing and waste/rewet; (e) all defaults are unsourced 'ballpark' per the README. Disclosed as editable, so a pro can fix the inputs, but the shipped defaults would under-bid stairs.

defects.what: Labour hours ignore coat count: baseCoats 1 vs 5 changes gallons/price (7082.50 vs 8125.16) but total hours stay 75.30. Each extra base coat is real application and dry-time labour; only the 'extraCoats' colour-change path adds hours.

Stair hours (0.4 h/tread) and area (4 sq ft/tread) are low versus trade practice and do not vary with method (screen vs full sand) or stain, so the headline 'stairs trap' product claim rests on a weak default; the 4 sq ft constant is not user-editable.
Optional-looking fields default to 0 via `?? 0` (wage, finishCost, overhead, supplies), so a blank input silently prices the job with free labour or finish instead of asking.
README and the how-much page say sand-and-stain is 'several hundred dollars more'; the tool gives +$1,415.90 over full-sand-poly on the default job.
Customer-facing comparison page leaks agent process ('Jobber's own site is not reachable from this session'); llms.txt links use the retired github.io address.

verdict: The arithmetic is right and well tested: four outputs recomputed by hand (default $7,603.83/75.30h, stained $9,019.73, 400 sq ft screen $2,036.11, stair share 16.9%) matched to the cent, margin is correctly applied to price, and two seeded mutations (markup instead of margin, floor instead of ceil gallons) were both caught by tests. All 102 tests pass across seven files and the claimed features (takeoff, proposal, share, copy summary, privacy tally) work with no stubs. It falls short of the senior-professional bar on fitness and domain, not correctness: the shipped hours are unsourced and low for stairs, coat count adds materials but no labour, and there is one blended labour rate, so a refinisher using the defaults would under-bid exactly the stair jobs the product is about. Small copy defects (vs-jobber agent-process text, stale llms.txt URLs, 'several hundred dollars') should be fixed forward. By the computed rule (correctness, claims, verification >= 3 and median >= 3) it meets the bar, and it is finished.
